hook_text: On a Saturday night in 1961, Berliners went to sleep in one city. On Sunday morning they woke up in two.
clip_script: Berlin, 1945. The war is over, and the winners cut Germany into four pieces. Berlin, deep in the Soviet piece, is cut into four too. In 1948 Stalin blocks every road and railway into West Berlin. Two million people, food for five weeks. So the West flies everything in. A plane every few minutes, for eleven months. Stalin gives up. Germany splits into two countries. In the west: a booming economy. In the east: shortages and secret police. Millions of East Germans leave, many through Berlin. Then, on the night of 13 August 1961, soldiers roll out barbed wire across the city. Within days, it is concrete. Families are cut off from each other overnight. Watchtowers. Guard dogs. A death strip. At least 140 people die trying to cross. For twenty-eight years, the Wall is the face of the Cold War.
visual_style: A map of Germany sliced into four coloured zones; transport planes landing in rapid sequence; a small parachute carrying sweets; soldiers unrolling barbed wire under streetlights; a concrete wall with a watchtower and a family waving across it.
pacing: Brisk through the zones and airlift, slowing at the night the Wall went up.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand the division of Germany and why the Berlin Wall was built.
